result: Cutting the number 42 bus would be a false economy that Leeds cannot afford. Every day, 3,100 people rely on this route, and it is no ordinary commuter line: it links two hospitals, carrying patients to appointments, staff to shifts, and families to the bedsides of people they love. Those are not journeys that can be easily postponed or replaced. A woman travelling to chemotherapy, a porter starting an early shift, a teenager visiting a grandparent on a ward: none of them has a convenient alternative if the service disappears. Taxis are costly, parking at both sites is notoriously limited, and many of these riders do not own a car. Remove the route and some will simply miss appointments, which means worse health outcomes and more expense for the NHS down the line. A council can find savings in many places, but a lifeline of this scale should not be among them. If the numbers on the spreadsheet look marginal, the answer is to improve frequency and reliability, not to abandon the people who depend on it. Leeds should keep the 42.
